views.name: products_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT p.id AS id,
       p.name AS name,
       p.group_id AS group_id,
       pg.name AS name_group,
       pa.sales_volume AS sales_volume,
       pa.abv AS abv
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN product_groups pg ON p.group_id = pg.id
LEFT JOIN product_alcohol pa ON p.id = pa.product_id

params.description: A denormalized product-level dimension that returns one row per product id with product attributes and the latest/stored alcohol attributes (sales_volume, abv) from product_alcohol and the product group name.
params.when_to_use: Enriching table-level facts or aggregates at the grain of a single product (product_id) where one row per product is required. | Lookup of product attributes (id, name, group_id, name_group) for use as join keys or labels in reports and downstream aggregations. | Reporting or display that needs the stored/linked product alcohol attributes (sales_volume, abv) as point-in-time attributes tied to the product dimension row.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining directly to transactional/event tables (orders, purchases, inventory lines) expecting aggregated measures to remain correct — doing so can duplicate rows and inflate aggregates because this view is one row per product; if the transactional table is many-to-one to product you must aggregate the transaction side before joining. | Using this view to compute product-level aggregates across time (trends, monthly totals) — product_alcohol.sales_volume appears as a stored attribute on this row, not as a time series; using it as a time-based metric will produce misleading results. | Assuming sales_volume is an aggregated metric across transactions: product_alcohol.sales_volume is taken directly from product_alcohol.product_id (no GROUP BY) and may represent a stored or latest value — re-aggregating raw transactions is required if you need true summed sales across orders/purchases. | Joining other one-to-many tables (for example purchases_enriched, orders_with_lines, inventory_by_location_product) without first aggregating the one-to-many side — doing so will multiply this view's rows and generate incorrectly high counts/sums.
params.output_schema: id: product id (derived from products.id) | name: product name (derived from products.name) | group_id: foreign key to product_groups (derived from products.group_id) | name_group: product group name (derived from product_groups.name via left join on products.group_id = product_groups.id) | sales_volume: stored sales_volume attribute for the product (derived from product_alcohol.sales_volume via left join on products.id = product_alcohol.product_id) | abv: alcohol by volume attribute for the product (derived from product_alcohol.abv via left join on products.id = product_alcohol.product_id)
params.grounded_columns: products.id | products.name | products.group_id | product_groups.id | product_groups.name | product_alcohol.product_id | product_alcohol.sales_volume | product_alcohol.abv
params.metric: sales_volume = product_alcohol.sales_volume  -- NOT an aggregate in this view; it's a direct column pulled by LEFT JOIN from product_alcohol | abv = product_alcohol.abv  -- NOT an aggregate in this view; it's a direct column pulled by LEFT JOIN from product_alcohol
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to a single-row-per-product dimension such as latest_purchase_per_product on id/product_id — safe because latest_purchase_per_product is ranked to one row per product so it will not multiply rows in this view. | cardinality-SAFE: join to product_groups on group_id = id — safe because product_groups is one row per product_group.id; joining will not duplicate product-level rows or their attributes. | do NOT join directly to purchases_enriched, orders_with_lines, inventory_by_location_product, ticker_daily, web_page_visit_counts, or any other one-to-many fact without first aggregating that fact to product-id level (e.g., sum(quantity) GROUP BY product_id) — those are one-to-many relative to products and will duplicate this view's product rows and thus inflate any measures taken from product_alcohol. | do NOT join to sibling AGG views that are aggregated at a different grain (monthly_sales_agg_by_product is monthly × product) unless you also include the corresponding time dimension in this view or reduce the AGG to product-only. Mismatched grains (product-only vs product+month) will lead to accidental cartesian-like expansion. | If you need to combine this view with many-to-many or multi-row per product sources, first reduce the other source to one row per product (e.g., latest metric per product, or an aggregated sum/count per product) to preserve cardinality safety.
params.comparison: use monthly_sales_agg_by_product instead when you need time-series aggregated sales (monthly) for each product — monthly_sales_agg_by_product provides pre-aggregated monthly measures, whereas products_dim only exposes a stored sales_volume attribute with no time dimension. | use latest_purchase_per_product when you require the most recent purchase event per product (timestamped row) rather than product-level static attributes — latest_purchase_per_product is ranked to one row per product representing latest purchase details. | use purchases_enriched or orders_with_lines when you need detailed transactional-level data (lines or enriched purchases) — those views contain the transactional grain and multiple rows per product, unlike this product-level dimension. | use inventory_by_location_product when you need inventory quantities broken down by location × product — inventory_by_location_product is aggregated to include location grain and should be used if location-level inventory detail is required, whereas products_dim has no location context.

views.description: One-row-per-product dimension combining product core attributes with group and alcohol metadata. Useful to enrich sales, purchases, inventory, and orders with product name, group name, sales_volume and abv. | Use for: Look up product attributes for reporting or joins (name, group, alcohol).; Compute sales/purchase/inventory rollups enriched with product metadata.; Filter products by group name or abv ranges.

views.name: monthly_sales_agg_by_product
views.body_sql:
SELECT product_id AS product_id,
       mth AS mth,
       SUM(qty) AS qty_total
FROM monthly_sales
GROUP BY product_id, mth

params.description: Provides monthly aggregated quantity sold per product (one row per product_id and month).
params.when_to_use: To report total quantity sold for a specific product in a specific month (time-series by product). | To join to product-level dimensions (product name, category) where you need monthly totals without further aggregation. | To compute month-over-month or trend metrics at the product-month grain (after ensuring joins do not multiply rows).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use for analyses that require a different grain (e.g., per-order, per-customer, per-location) — joining order- or line-level tables without re-aggregation will create double-counting because this view is already aggregated to product_id × mth. | Do not use when you need distinct counts of orders or customers: this view aggregates quantity only and does not contain order_id or customer_id; attempting to derive counts from qty_total is incorrect. | Do not use to compute cumulative or running totals across months without performing the appropriate windowing outside this view — this view only provides per-month totals and lacks ordering or cumulative logic. | Do not join to one-to-many detail tables (e.g., purchases_enriched, orders_with_lines, inventory_by_location_product) without re-aggregating the joined result back to product_id × mth, because such joins will multiply qty_total and cause silently-wrong sums.
params.output_schema: product_id: product identifier for the product (derived from monthly_sales.product_id) | mth: month identifier (same value as monthly_sales.mth; represents the month grouping key used in aggregation) | qty_total: SUM(qty) aggregated over all rows in monthly_sales for the given product_id and mth (derived from monthly_sales.qty)
params.metric: qty_total = SUM(monthly_sales.qty) GROUP BY monthly_sales.product_id, monthly_sales.mth
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_dim on product_id — safe because products_dim is expected to be one-row-per-product_id (a dimension), so it will not duplicate qty_total. | Safe to join to any other one-row-per-product table or view (e.g., latest_purchase_per_product if that view is one-row-per-product) provided the join key is product_id and the sibling view's grain is one row per product_id; these joins will not multiply measures. | Do NOT join directly to purchases_enriched or orders_with_lines without re-aggregating those tables to product_id × mth first — they are order/line-level (one-to-many relative to this view) and will inflate qty_total if joined without aggregation. | Do NOT join to inventory_by_location_product without aggregating inventory_by_location_product up to product_id × mth (if needed) because inventory_by_location_product is aggregated by location × product and can create many rows per product_id, duplicating measures. | If you must combine this view with a one-to-many table, perform the join from the detail side and then re-aggregate: e.g., FROM monthly_sales_agg_by_product AS m JOIN orders_with_lines AS o ON m.product_id = o.product_id AND m.mth = o.mth; then SELECT m.product_id, m.mth, SUM(o.qty) (or appropriate metric) — avoid taking m.qty_total * something from multiplied rows without correcting for duplication.
params.comparison: use products_dim instead when you only need product attributes (name, category) and not monthly quantity totals — products_dim is a product attribute dimension (JOIN) and contains one row per product_id. | use purchases_enriched when you need order- or customer-level context (timestamps, customer_id, order_id) and plan to compute metrics at that finer grain — purchases_enriched is line/order-level (JOIN) and contains detail rows required for order-level analyses. | use inventory_by_location_product when you need inventory quantities split by location as that view provides location-level aggregation; monthly_sales_agg_by_product is product-month totals and does not capture location details. | use orders_with_lines when you need to analyze individual order lines or compute metrics that require order-level identifiers; monthly_sales_agg_by_product aggregates away order-level detail. | use ticker_daily or web_page_visit_counts when your analysis is time-series at a different domain (financial ticks or web events) — monthly_sales_agg_by_product is specific to product sales quantities per month.

views.description: Aggregated monthly sales measures per product and month. Produces one row per product_id+mth with total qty. Useful as a canonical sales fact for time-series analyses and comparisons to budgets. | Use for: Monthly time series of sales for products.; Compare monthly_sales to monthly_budget or compute growth rates.; Join to products_dim to get product names for reporting.

views.name: purchases_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT pur.id AS id,
       pur.purchased AS purchased,
       pur.brewery_id AS brewery_id,
       b.name AS name_brewery,
       pur.product_id AS product_id,
       p.name AS name_product,
       pur.qty AS qty,
       pur.cost AS cost
FROM purchases pur
LEFT JOIN breweries b ON pur.brewery_id = b.id
LEFT JOIN products p ON pur.product_id = p.id

params.description: One-row-per-purchase record combining purchases with brewery and product descriptive attributes.
params.when_to_use: To get detailed purchase-level records including product and brewery names. | To build reports or extracts where each row should correspond to a single purchase (grain = purchases.id). | To join purchase rows to other one-row-per-purchase or one-row-per-order datasets safely (see composition).
params.when_not_to_use: When you need aggregated metrics (totals, averages) across products, breweries, time windows or customers — this view is at the raw purchase row grain and does not perform aggregation; using it directly to compute aggregates without grouping will produce incorrect results (mis-aggregation). | When you need one-row-per-product (product-level) or one-row-per-brewery summaries — joining this view to product- or brewery-level aggregations without performing aggregation on purchases will double-count or mis-count because there can be many purchases per product or brewery (grain mismatch). | When you need the latest purchase per product or per brewery — this view contains all purchases; use a RANK/deduplicated view (e.g., latest_purchase_per_product) instead to avoid multiple rows per product. | When constructing cohort/time-windowed metrics: do not treat this as pre-aggregated by time; aggregations must be computed explicitly (cohort/aggregation anti-pattern).
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the purchase row (derived from purchases.id). One row in this view equals one purchase. | purchased: timestamp or date/time when the purchase occurred (derived from purchases.purchased). | brewery_id: foreign key referencing the brewery associated with the purchase (derived from purchases.brewery_id). | name_brewery: brewery name (derived from breweries.name via LEFT JOIN on purchases.brewery_id = breweries.id). NULL if no matching brewery. | product_id: foreign key referencing the product purchased (derived from purchases.product_id). | name_product: product name (derived from products.name via LEFT JOIN on purchases.product_id = products.id). NULL if no matching product. | qty: quantity purchased (derived from purchases.qty). | cost: cost of the purchase (derived from purchases.cost).
params.grounded_columns: purchases.id | purchases.purchased | purchases.brewery_id | purchases.product_id | purchases.qty | purchases.cost | breweries.id | breweries.name | products.id | products.name
params.metric: qty = purchases.qty (base column, not an aggregate in this view) | cost = purchases.cost (base column, not an aggregate in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to brewery-level dimension (breweries or a brewery_dim) on purchases.brewery_id = breweries.id — safe because breweries is one-row-per-brewery; joining will not multiply purchase rows or purchase-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product-level dimension (products or products_dim) on purchases.product_id = products.id — safe because products is one-row-per-product; joining will not multiply purchase rows or purchase-level measures. | do NOT join this view to an orders_with_lines (one-to-many) or any other one-to-many table keyed to purchase.id without first aggregating those tables to one-row-per-purchase — otherwise you will multiply purchase rows and overcount qty/cost. | do NOT join this view directly to aggregate views like monthly_sales_agg_by_product or inventory_by_location_product expecting to preserve purchase-level measures — these are aggregated at different grains (product-month or product-location) and will require explicit grouping/aggregation and careful key alignment to avoid incorrect duplication or loss of granularity. | When joining to sibling views that are at coarser grains (AGG), join patterns should be: either (a) aggregate this view up to the sibling's grain first (group by product_id / month / brewery_id as needed) or (b) join the sibling aggregated view to this view on the aggregated keys with care to avoid multiplying rows. Example safe approach: compute product-month totals from purchases_enriched by grouping on product_id and month(purchased), then join to monthly_sales_agg_by_product by product+month to compare metrics.
params.comparison: use products_dim when you only need product attributes and do not want purchase rows — products_dim is a product-level JOIN and will return one row per product (coarser grain than this view). | use monthly_sales_agg_by_product when you need aggregated sales metrics by month+product (pre-aggregated) instead of raw purchase rows; it avoids manual grouping and prevents mis-aggregation mistakes. | use latest_purchase_per_product when you only need the most recent purchase per product — this view contains all purchases so it would return multiple rows per product and require additional deduplication. | use orders_with_lines when you need order-level grouping with line-item detail at an order grain that differs from purchases.id (orders_with_lines may represent a different business entity/grain).

views.description: One-row-per-purchase event enriched with brewery and product descriptive fields for easy consumption by reporting and aggregation layers. | Use for: Analyze purchase costs and volumes by brewery or product.; Time-series of purchases, e.g., monthly or per supplier.; Join with inventory or products_dim to reconcile receipts.

views.name: inventory_by_location_product
views.body_sql:
SELECT location_id AS location_id,
       product_id AS product_id,
       SUM(qty) AS qty_onhand,
       MIN(id) AS sample_inventory_id
FROM inventory
GROUP BY location_id, product_id

params.description: Per-location, per-product current on-hand inventory totals (sum of qty) and a sample inventory row id for that location-product.
params.when_to_use: Report or dashboard needing the current total quantity on hand for each product at each location. | Joining inventory totals to dimensions (e.g., product or location) to show inventory by product/location without double-counting. | Filtering to a subset of locations or products and aggregating further (e.g., roll-up to location or product totals) — safe because source grain matches aggregation keys.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need row-level inventory transactions or change history (this view is aggregated; it loses individual inventory transaction rows). | Do not use when you require a deterministic representative inventory row (sample_inventory_id is MIN(id) and only a heuristic pointer to a row, not necessarily the canonical or latest row). | Do not use when you need inventory over time or per-cohort (this view has no date/time dimension; aggregating across time will silently hide temporal variation). | Do not use when joining to one-to-many tables without re-aggregating: joining to transactional tables (e.g., inventory transactions or order lines) directly will multiply qty_onhand and produce wrong sums.
params.output_schema: location_id: identifier of the inventory storage location; sourced from inventory.location_id | product_id: identifier of the product/SKU at that location; sourced from inventory.product_id | qty_onhand: total quantity on hand for that (location_id, product_id) pair — derived as SUM(inventory.qty) | sample_inventory_id: an example inventory row id for this (location_id, product_id) pair — derived as MIN(inventory.id) and intended only as a referential pointer, not authoritative
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_dim on product_id — safe because products_dim is expected to be one-row-per-product, so this view's measures (qty_onhand) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a location dimension (if present) on location_id — safe because a location dimension is one-row-per-location. | DO NOT join directly to inventory (the raw transactional table) or any other one-to-many detail tables on (location_id, product_id) without first aggregating those detail tables to the same grain; doing so will multiply rows and inflate qty_onhand. | DO NOT join to sibling aggregations that are at a finer grain (e.g., time-series of inventory) without aligning grain and re-aggregating, because you will produce incorrect counts or double-counting. | If you need to combine with orders_with_lines or purchases_enriched (which are joins that may be at order/line grain), aggregate those sources to (location_id, product_id) first, then join — otherwise orders or purchases with multiple lines per product/location will duplicate inventory measures.
params.comparison: use products_dim when you need product attributes (name, category) — it is a dimension/join view containing product attributes, whereas this view contains aggregated inventory measures. | use latest_purchase_per_product when you need the last purchase record for a product — that sibling is a RANK view focused on recency, whereas inventory_by_location_product gives aggregated on-hand totals by location and product. | use monthly_sales_agg_by_product when you need time-bucketed sales metrics at product grain — monthly_sales_agg_by_product is time-aggregated (by month) and product-level; inventory_by_location_product is current on-hand by location and product and has no time dimension. | use orders_with_lines or purchases_enriched when you need transactional/order-level details (order ids, line ids, vendor info) — those are JOIN views at transactional grain and will contain many rows per product/location; inventory_by_location_product is pre-aggregated and should not be replaced by transactional joins without re-aggregation.

views.description: Current inventory quantities aggregated by location and product (one row per location_id+product_id). Useful to compute on-hand across locations and join to locations or products for dispatch/planning. | Use for: Compute stock-on-hand by location or product for replenishment.; Join to locations and products_dim to build picking lists.; Compare on-hand to product_minimums or monthly_budget.

views.name: orders_with_lines
views.body_sql:
SELECT ol.id AS id,
       ol.order_id AS order_id,
       o.customer_id AS customer_id,
       c.name AS name_customer,
       o.ordered AS ordered,
       o.delivery AS delivery,
       ol.product_id AS product_id,
       p.name AS name_product,
       ol.qty AS qty,
       ol.amount AS amount
FROM orderlines ol
LEFT JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.id
LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN products p ON ol.product_id = p.id

params.description: A row-level denormalized listing of order lines with their parent order, customer, and product attributes — suitable for row-level reporting, export, and drilling into individual order-line details.
params.when_to_use: Listing or exporting individual order lines with order, customer, and product context (e.g., show every line item in an order with customer name and product name). | Drilling from aggregated sales metrics down to the underlying order-line detail for investigation or reconciliation. | Joining to event-level or transactional datasets at the order-line grain for enrichment (provided joins are cardinality-safe — see composition).
params.when_not_to_use: Aggregating across orders/products/customers to produce metrics like daily sales, because this view is at the order-line grain and does not pre-aggregate — using it directly for high-level aggregates is possible but you must aggregate correctly (GROUP BY at the order-line level) to avoid mis-count. | Creating cohort or customer-level analyses that expect one-row-per-customer: joining this view directly to customer-level tables without first deduplicating or aggregating will multiply customer counts (grain mismatch). | Joining to other one-to-many tables (e.g., another orderlines-like table) without re-aggregation first — such joins will produce row multiplication and incorrectly inflated measures (quantity/amount will be duplicated).
params.output_schema: id: unique orderline identifier; sourced from orderlines.id (ol.id). This is the view's declared grain. | order_id: foreign key to orders; sourced from orderlines.order_id (ol.order_id). | customer_id: foreign key to customers owning the order; sourced from orders.customer_id (o.customer_id). | name_customer: customer's name; sourced from customers.name (c.name) via orders.customer_id -> customers.id. | ordered: order-level ordered timestamp/date; sourced from orders.ordered (o.ordered). | delivery: order-level delivery timestamp/date; sourced from orders.delivery (o.delivery). | product_id: foreign key to products; sourced from orderlines.product_id (ol.product_id). | name_product: product name; sourced from products.name (p.name) via orderlines.product_id -> products.id. | qty: quantity at the order-line level; sourced from orderlines.qty (ol.qty). | amount: monetary amount for the order-line; sourced from orderlines.amount (ol.amount).
params.grounded_columns: orderlines.id | orderlines.order_id | orderlines.product_id | orderlines.qty | orderlines.amount | orders.id | orders.customer_id | orders.ordered | orders.delivery | customers.id | customers.name | products.id | products.name
params.metric: qty = raw measure from orderlines.qty (no aggregation in this view; sum/avg must be performed by consumer when aggregating). | amount = raw measure from orderlines.amount (no aggregation in this view; sum/avg must be performed by consumer when aggregating).
params.composition: Safe: join to products_dim on product_id = products_dim.id — products_dim is a product-level (one-row-per-product) dimension so it will not duplicate order-line rows or measures. | Safe: join to employees_hierarchy on employees_hierarchy.id = orders.<employee_id> (if present) only if employees_hierarchy is one-row-per-employee; confirm that join key is unique in employees_hierarchy to avoid duplication. | Do NOT join directly to monthly_sales_agg_by_product (an aggregated view) expecting row-level detail — monthly_sales_agg_by_product is already aggregated and represents different grain (month/product); combine by joining on product_id and month keys after aligning grains, or aggregate this view to month/product first before joining. | Do NOT join to sibling joins that are one-to-many relative to orderlines (for example, another transactional log with multiple events per orderline) without first aggregating that other dataset to the orderline (id) level — otherwise qty and amount will be multiplied. | When joining to purchases_enriched or latest_purchase_per_product: verify those siblings are one-row-per-product (or one-row-per-key) before joining on product_id. If they are one-to-many (e.g., purchase history), aggregate or pick a single row (e.g., latest) to avoid duplicating order-line rows. | When producing aggregates from this view (e.g., total sales per customer), always aggregate qty/amount using SUM(...) grouped by the intended keys; do not rely on COUNT(id) as a measure of quantity or amount.
params.comparison: use products_dim instead when you only need product-level attributes for many products without order-line detail — products_dim is product-grain and avoids transferring many order-line rows. | use monthly_sales_agg_by_product instead when you need pre-computed aggregated sales by month and product (it has pre-aggregated sums and reduces compute and risk of double-counting over time windows). | use purchases_enriched when your primary need is enriched purchase-level data (if purchases_enriched is at purchase grain and not order-line grain); choose it if you need purchase-centric attributes rather than order-line detail. | use latest_purchase_per_product when you only need the single latest purchase per product (it provides a rank-based reduction to one row per product) rather than all order lines referencing that product. | do not use inventory_by_location_product for transactional sales metrics — inventory_by_location_product is aggregated to inventory counts by location/product and serves a different analytical purpose.

views.description: Denormalized order-line level detail: one row per orderline including order header and customer info. Useful for sales reporting, customer order histories and fulfillment analyses. | Use for: Order line level revenue and quantity analyses by customer, product, or date.; Build customer order histories or compute fulfillment KPIs.; Feed into picking/picking_list processes and reconcile with picking_line.

views.name: ticker_daily
views.body_sql:
SELECT symbol AS symbol,
       day AS day,
       AVG(price) AS price_avg
FROM ticker
GROUP BY symbol, day

params.description: Daily average price per traded symbol — answers what the average observed ticker price was for each symbol on each day.
params.when_to_use: Report or chart showing the average price of each symbol per day (time series at daily grain). | Joining to dimension tables (e.g., product/asset metadata) on symbol to enrich daily-average prices without changing measures. | Filtering or comparing daily average prices across symbols or date ranges.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining directly to a one-to-many table (e.g., an orders or trades table that contains multiple lines per symbol per day) without re-aggregating — this will multiply rows and silently inflate or distort averages. | Using it to compute intraday metrics (minute/hour grain) — the view is aggregated to day; using it as if it were raw tick data or to compute within-day variability will lose information. | Attempting to compute counts of underlying ticks (or distinct tick events) from price_avg — you cannot recover underlying counts or distributions from an average, so cohort or frequency analysis based on per-tick counts is incorrect. | Merging this view across non-aligned time grains (e.g., monthly) without re-aggregation — aggregating averages without weighting by underlying counts may yield biased monthly averages.
params.output_schema: symbol: the traded symbol identifier, derived from ticker.symbol | day: the calendar day (date) that groups observations, derived from ticker.day | price_avg: the arithmetic mean of price values for the given symbol and day, defined as AVG(ticker.price)
params.metric: price_avg = AVG(ticker.price)  -- average (mean) of price over all ticker rows sharing the same (symbol, day)
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-symbol dimension (e.g., products_dim) on ticker_daily.symbol — safe because products_dim is one-to-one per symbol, so this view's per-day measures are not duplicated. | Join to a one-row-per-day dimension (if present) on ticker_daily.day — safe because day is one-row-per-date, preserving measures. | Do NOT join ticker_daily to any table or view that is one-to-many from (symbol, day) (for example, orders_with_lines or purchases_enriched if they contain multiple rows per symbol per day) without first aggregating that other source to the same (symbol, day) grain. Joining a (symbol, day) aggregated view to a detail table with multiple rows per (symbol, day) will multiply rows and incorrectly change aggregates. | If you need to combine with other aggregated metrics (e.g., totals or counts) ensure the other metric is aggregated to (symbol, day) as well, or perform a proper weighted aggregation when rolling up to coarser grains (e.g., month) using underlying counts when available. | When enriching with sibling aggregated views (e.g., inventory_by_location_product or monthly_sales_agg_by_product), only combine if those siblings are aggregated to exactly (symbol, day) or else re-aggregate/align grains first to avoid silent mis-counts.
params.comparison: use products_dim instead when you only need static product/asset attributes for a symbol — products_dim provides descriptive fields and should be used as the dimension in joins (ticker_daily is a metric/aggregation). | use monthly_sales_agg_by_product instead when you need monthly sales totals by product rather than daily average prices — monthly_sales_agg_by_product is aggregated at a monthly grain and likely contains sales-specific measures that ticker_daily does not. | use purchases_enriched or orders_with_lines when you need transactional or line-level purchase/order details (one-to-many transactional data) rather than a pre-aggregated daily price; but if you join them to ticker_daily, aggregate the transactional side to (symbol, day) first to preserve correctness. | use latest_purchase_per_product when you need the most recent purchase per product (rank/top-N) — that view provides a different analytic grain (latest row per product) and is not a per-day time series.

views.description: Canonical daily ticker price per symbol and day. Aggregates in case of duplicates and exposes a simple price measure for time-series analyses or joins to stock. | Use for: Time-series stock price analysis and joins to stock for company-level reports.; Compute returns, moving averages, and compare with business events.

views.name: web_page_visit_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT app_id AS app_id,
       page_no AS page_no,
       date(visit_time) AS day,
       COUNT(*) AS visits
FROM web_page_visits
GROUP BY app_id, page_no, date(visit_time)

params.description: Daily counts of page visits per application and page (how many raw visit events occurred for each app_id × page_no × day).
params.when_to_use: Answering how many visit events occurred to a specific page (page_no) of an application (app_id) on a given calendar date (day). | Feeding a dashboard or alert that needs daily traffic volumes per page (e.g., top pages by visits per day). | As a pre-aggregated input to further analysis that operates at the app_id × page_no × day grain (e.g., time-series smoothing, daily trendlines).
params.when_not_to_use: Joining to tables that expand cardinality (one-to-many) without re-aggregation — this will multiply visit counts because this view already returns COUNT(*) per app_id,page_no,day. Always re-aggregate after joining one-to-many detail. | Estimating unique users or devices — visits is a raw event COUNT(*) and does not deduplicate by user_id or device_id; using it as 'unique visitors' yields inflated counts. | Using it as a session-level or visitor-level source — the grain is event counts per day, not sessions or users. Aggregating to session/user requires joining with session/user tables and re-aggregating at the new grain. | Mixing with cohorts by visit_time timestamp ranges without aligning the date() truncation — if other data uses different date-truncation or timezone logic, you may silently mis-assign events to different days.
params.output_schema: app_id: application identifier — derived from base column web_page_visits.app_id | page_no: page number/identifier within the app — derived from base column web_page_visits.page_no | day: calendar date of the visit (DATE) — derived from date(web_page_visits.visit_time) | visits: count of raw visit events for the app_id × page_no × day — derived from COUNT(*) over rows in web_page_visits grouped by app_id, page_no, date(visit_time)
params.metric: visits = COUNT(*) grouped by (app_id, page_no, date(visit_time))
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like, one-row-per-key tables/views on matching keys — safe examples: | join to products_dim on a matching key only if products_dim is one-row-per-(app_id,page_no) and you are adding descriptive attributes; safe because products_dim will not duplicate this view's rows or measures. | join to web_devices_totals on (app_id) only if web_devices_totals is one-row-per-app_id — safe because it will not multiply visit counts when joined on app_id. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., orders_with_lines, purchases_enriched, inventory_by_location_product) without re-aggregation because those joins will multiply visits. For example, joining to orders_with_lines (multiple order lines per order) will replicate a single visit row for every matching order line and inflate the visits measure. | If you must combine with a one-to-many child, perform aggregation after the join at the intended target grain (for example: SELECT app_id, page_no, day, SUM(visits) FROM (web_page_visit_counts JOIN child) GROUP BY app_id, page_no, day) or instead join web_page_visit_counts to a pre-aggregated version of the child that is one-row-per-join-key. | Avoid joining on keys that do not uniquely identify rows in this view (the unique grain is app_id × page_no × day). Joining on only app_id (dropping page_no and/or day) is allowed if the other side is one-row-per-app_id — otherwise re-aggregate or restrict keys to preserve correctness.
params.comparison: use products_dim instead when you need descriptive product/page attributes rather than counts — products_dim is a JOIN (dimension) and contains descriptive fields at its own grain. | use web_devices_totals instead when you need aggregated device-level totals per app (not per page per day) — web_devices_totals is normalized/aggregated at a different grain (likely app or device) and is appropriate when page_no/day breakdown is not required. | use monthly_sales_agg_by_product or ticker_daily when you need sales/ticker financial aggregates rather than web visit events — those sibling AGG views aggregate different base tables and answer different business questions. | use purchases_enriched or orders_with_lines when you need transaction/order level detail; they are JOINs that provide transactional context rather than raw web visit counts. | use latest_purchase_per_product when you need latest-event rank semantics per product; that RANK view addresses recency, whereas web_page_visit_counts is a simple event count by date.

views.description: Counts of web page visits per app_id, page_no and day. Useful to analyze traffic trends, join to web_pages for friendly_url and compute daily metrics. | Use for: Daily traffic per page for engagement or capacity planning.; Join to web_pages to get friendly_url and to web_counter_hist for validation.

views.name: employees_hierarchy
views.body_sql:
SELECT id AS id,
       name AS name,
       title AS title,
       supervisor_id AS supervisor_id,
       id AS root_id,
       name AS root_name,
       0 AS depth,
       CAST(id AS TEXT) AS path
FROM employees
WHERE supervisor_id IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT e.id AS id,
       e.name AS name,
       e.title AS title,
       e.supervisor_id AS supervisor_id,
       h.root_id AS root_id,
       h.root_name AS root_name,
       h.depth + 1 AS depth,
       h.path || '>' || CAST(e.id AS TEXT) AS path
FROM employees e
JOIN employees_hierarchy h ON e.supervisor_id = h.id

params.description: A recursive employee hierarchy view that returns every employee with their top-level root (CEO) id/name, depth in that root's tree, and the path of ids from root to the employee.
params.when_to_use: Show reporting chain for each employee (who is the root/CEO for this employee and how deep they sit). | Build organizational tree visualizations or breadcrumbs (path field) from root to each employee. | Filter or group employees by top-level organization (root_id/root_name) or depth.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view directly to transactional fact tables and then summing measures from those facts without re-aggregation — because this view is dimensional (one row per employee per root) and joining to many-to-one or one-to-many facts will multiply fact rows if you then sum without first aggregating the fact to employee level. | Using this view to compute measures that require current-time snapshots of supervisory relationships when the underlying employees table contains historical rows (temporal/cohort analyses) — the view reflects the current employees table rows only. | Assuming path is a stable key for grouping across datasets — path is a text concatenation of ids and is not normalized; grouping by it may produce unexpected results if ids are cast/represented differently downstream. | Treating depth as a continuous numeric measure to average across managers without considering varying tree shapes — averaging depth across roots/cohorts can be misleading (cohort/aggregation anti-pattern).
params.output_schema: id: employee id (employees.id) — the unique identifier for the employee row referenced in the employees table. | name: employee name (employees.name) — the name column from the employees table for this employee. | title: employee title/role (employees.title) — the title column from the employees table for this employee. | supervisor_id: immediate manager's employee id (employees.supervisor_id) — the direct supervisor; NULL for root rows. | root_id: top-level root employee id for this employee's tree (derived from employees.id in root rows and propagated via recursive join to employees_hierarchy.root_id) — equals id when the employee is a root (supervisor_id IS NULL). | root_name: top-level root employee name (derived from employees.name in root rows and propagated via recursion) — name of the root row. | depth: integer depth from the root (0 for root rows) — computed as 0 for root rows and incremented by 1 for each level in recursion (h.depth + 1). | path: text path of ids from root to this employee (constructed as CAST(id AS TEXT) for root and concatenated '>' delimited via h.path || '>' || CAST(e.id AS TEXT) in recursion) — a textual breadcrumb of the id chain.
params.grounded_columns: employees.id | employees.name | employees.title | employees.supervisor_id | employees_hierarchy.id | employees_hierarchy.root_id | employees_hierarchy.root_name | employees_hierarchy.depth | employees_hierarchy.path
params.metric: depth = 0 for rows where employees.supervisor_id IS NULL; otherwise depth = parent.depth + 1 (integer increment per level). | path = CAST(id AS TEXT) for root rows; otherwise path = parent.path || '>' || CAST(current.id AS TEXT) (text concatenation of ids from root to current). | root_id = id for root rows; otherwise root_id = parent's root_id (propagated from the recursive anchor). | root_name = name for root rows; otherwise root_name = parent's root_name (propagated).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to a one-row-per-employee dimension (e.g., products_dim is NOT appropriate because it's products, not employees) — more generally, join to views/tables that are 1:1 with employees on employees.id (or this view's id) without introducing multiplication. Example: join employees_hierarchy AS eh ON eh.id = other_table.employee_id is safe if other_table has at most one row per employee (one-to-one). | safe: join to normalized employee-level lookup tables (one row per employee) on id or to other single-row-per-root resources on root_id — these joins will not duplicate the hierarchy rows. | not safe: do NOT join employees_hierarchy directly to one-to-many tables (e.g., orders_with_lines, purchases_enriched, monthly_sales_agg_by_product if per-product-month instead of per-employee) without first aggregating the many-side to employee-level. Joining to a one-to-many will multiply rows and cause inflated counts/sums (measure duplication). | not safe: do NOT join to sibling AGG views that are aggregated at different grains (e.g., ticker_daily aggregated by date/instrument) unless you re-aggregate or join on keys that align the grains exactly. Mismatched grain leads to silently wrong aggregates. | recommendation: if you need totals (counts, sums) per employee/root, aggregate the fact table first to the same grain as this view (employee id or root_id) before joining, or join and then GROUP BY the hierarchy keys while re-aggregating measures.
params.comparison: use orders_with_lines instead when you need order-level detail including line items and are joining products or sales facts to employees only after proper aggregation — orders_with_lines provides fact-level joinability but is one-to-many and must be aggregated before combining with this hierarchy. | use monthly_sales_agg_by_product instead when you need pre-aggregated product-month sales; do NOT substitute employees_hierarchy for product dimension joins — they cover different domains (employees vs products). | use latest_purchase_per_product when you need the most recent purchase per product (ranked result) rather than an employee reporting structure — it's a different grain (product-level) and purpose. | use web_devices_totals or web_page_visit_counts when you need web analytics aggregates; these are aggregated at visitor/device/page grains and should be joined only after aligning grain to employees (e.g., if linking by employee as a user id, ensure those web aggregates are computed per-employee first).

views.description: Recursive employee reporting chain: each row is an employee-supervisor hop allowing construction of full reporting paths. Useful for org chart explorations, span-of-control, and manager-level rollups. | Use for: Build full reporting chains from top-level managers down.; Compute depth or path-based analyses like span-of-control.

views.name: web_devices_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT day AS day,
       pc AS pc,
       tablet AS tablet,
       phone AS phone,
       (COALESCE(pc,0) + COALESCE(tablet,0) + COALESCE(phone,0)) AS total_devices
FROM web_devices

params.description: Daily counts of web device types (pc, tablet, phone) and their per-day total across the website.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of visits/sessions/records per device type for a specific day or a date range (aggregation at day grain). | Plot daily device-type trends (pc vs tablet vs phone) or compute device mix per day. | Join to a calendar or date-dimension on day to align with other daily metrics.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view to a table that is one-to-many per day (for example raw page views or orders_with_lines) without first aggregating that table to the day grain — doing so will multiply device counts and produce inflated totals (aggregation/grain mismatch). | Using this view to answer user-level/cohort questions (for example, "unique users by device") because the view contains device-type counts at the day level, not distinct user identifiers — this will cause mis-counts if interpreted as distinct users. | Attempting to aggregate by any grain finer than day (for example hour or session) because the source is daily and cannot be split reliably — this would silently produce incorrect per-hour values. | Treating the total_devices column as an independent metric from its parts when some device columns are NULL — the total is a sum of pc, tablet, phone with COALESCE to 0, so omitting that behaviour when reusing may lead to different totals.
params.output_schema: day: the date representing the day of the counts; derived from web_devices.day | pc: integer/number of the pc device-type count for that day; derived from web_devices.pc | tablet: integer/number of the tablet device-type count for that day; derived from web_devices.tablet | phone: integer/number of the phone device-type count for that day; derived from web_devices.phone | total_devices: integer/number equal to COALESCE(pc,0) + COALESCE(tablet,0) + COALESCE(phone,0); computed in this view from the three device columns
params.metric: pc = web_devices.pc | tablet = web_devices.tablet | phone = web_devices.phone | total_devices = COALESCE(web_devices.pc, 0) + COALESCE(web_devices.tablet, 0) + COALESCE(web_devices.phone, 0)
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to date/calendar or other one-row-per-day dimensions on web_devices.day — safe because web_devices (and therefore this view) is one row per day so measures are not duplicated. | Join to a one-to-one or many-to-one dimension (for example a daily traffic_summary dimension keyed by day) is safe because it does not increase the row multiplicity for the day grain. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views keyed by day (for example raw page_view events, orders_with_lines, web_page_visit_counts if it is at a finer grain) without first aggregating those tables to day. Such joins will multiply this view's per-day device counts and produce inflated totals. | If you need to combine this view with another one-to-many dataset, first aggregate that dataset to day (e.g., SUM or COUNT grouped by day) and then join on day to preserve correct totals. | Avoid joining to unaggregated sibling JOIN views that expand rows per day (e.g., orders_with_lines) unless you re-aggregate after the join to restore the day grain.
params.comparison: use web_page_visit_counts instead when you need other daily visit/site metrics (page views, sessions) alongside device counts — web_page_visit_counts may contain other aggregates that are computed differently or at a different event definition. | use web_demographics_unpivot when you need device counts in a long/unpivoted shape (device_type, count) rather than wide columns (pc/tablet/phone) — that view is reshaped for per-device-type analysis. | use latest_purchase_per_product or orders_with_lines when you need order-level or purchase-level details — those sibling views provide event/transaction-level rows rather than daily device aggregates and are therefore different grain and purpose. | use ticker_daily or monthly_sales_agg_by_product when you need time-series aggregates for other domains (financials, sales) because those are designed for their domain; do not conflate domain aggregates without confirming consistent event definitions and grains.

views.description: Normalized daily device totals and a derived total_devices measure. One row per day with device breakdown and total. Useful as canonical input for traffic or cross-day comparisons. | Use for: Daily device mix and totals for analytics dashboards.; Join to web_demographics or web_page_visits for deeper segmentation.

views.name: web_demographics_unpivot
views.body_sql:
SELECT day AS day,
       'M' AS letter,
       'tw' AS channel_shortcut,
       m_tw_cnt AS cnt,
       m_tw_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day AS day,
       'M' AS letter,
       'fb' AS channel_shortcut,
       m_fb_cnt AS cnt,
       m_fb_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day AS day,
       'F' AS letter,
       'tw' AS channel_shortcut,
       f_tw_cnt AS cnt,
       f_tw_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day AS day,
       'F' AS letter,
       'fb' AS channel_shortcut,
       f_fb_cnt AS cnt,
       f_fb_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics

params.description: Provides a day × sex-letter × channel (tw/fb) reshaped count and quantity metrics derived from the wide web_demographics table.
params.when_to_use: Report or chart that needs a row-per-day/per-sex/per-channel view of counts and quantities (e.g., time series by channel and sex). | Feeding downstream transforms or visuals that expect a normalized (tall) form rather than the wide web_demographics table. | Joining to dimension tables (e.g., channel lookup, date dimension, sex dimension) where a single row per day×sex×channel is appropriate.
params.when_not_to_use: Joining to a one-to-many fact-like table (e.g., orders_with_lines) without re-aggregation — doing so will multiply cnt/qty because this view already represents aggregated metrics at day×letter×channel granularity. | As a source for user-level/cohort-level analysis that assumes row-level events — this view contains aggregated counts (cnt) and quantities (qty), not individual events or user ids. | For analyses that require channels other than 'tw' or 'fb' or letters other than 'M'/'F' — the view only exposes those four combinations and would silently omit others. | When you need to compute new aggregates by grouping on additional dimensions present in web_demographics (e.g., region) that were not preserved here — grouping downstream may produce incorrect totals if additional dimensions existed in the original table but were dropped here.
params.output_schema: day: date (day) — sourced from web_demographics.day; represents the calendar day for the aggregated metrics. | letter: text — literal 'M' or 'F' assigned in the view to represent male/female sex categories; not a derived column from web_demographics other than by choice of literal mapping. | channel_shortcut: text — literal 'tw' or 'fb' assigned in the view to indicate Twitter or Facebook channel; not derived from a base column other than the chosen literal in each UNION branch. | cnt: integer/number — sourced from one of web_demographics.m_tw_cnt, m_fb_cnt, f_tw_cnt, f_fb_cnt depending on the UNION branch; represents the aggregated count metric at day×letter×channel. | qty: numeric/number — sourced from one of web_demographics.m_tw_qty, m_fb_qty, f_tw_qty, f_fb_qty depending on the UNION branch; represents the aggregated quantity metric at day×letter×channel.
params.grounded_columns: web_demographics.day | web_demographics.m_tw_cnt | web_demographics.m_tw_qty | web_demographics.m_fb_cnt | web_demographics.m_fb_qty | web_demographics.f_tw_cnt | web_demographics.f_tw_qty | web_demographics.f_fb_cnt | web_demographics.f_fb_qty
params.metric: cnt = direct passthrough of the appropriate base column (web_demographics.m_tw_cnt | m_fb_cnt | f_tw_cnt | f_fb_cnt) depending on (letter, channel_shortcut). No additional aggregation is performed in this view. | qty = direct passthrough of the appropriate base column (web_demographics.m_tw_qty | m_fb_qty | f_tw_qty | f_fb_qty) depending on (letter, channel_shortcut). No additional aggregation is performed in this view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a date dimension on day (this view is one-row-per-day×letter×channel, so joining to a one-row-per-day dimension will not duplicate measures). Example: JOIN date_dim d ON web_demographics_unpivot.day = d.day — safe because date_dim is one-row-per-day. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a small dimension that is one-row-per-letter (sex) or one-row-per-channel on letter or channel_shortcut respectively — safe because those are many-to-one from this view to the dimension. | do NOT join directly to orders_with_lines, purchases_enriched, or any other table/view that is one-to-many relative to day (or day×letter×channel) without first aggregating that other table to day×letter×channel. Doing so will multiply cnt and qty because this view already contains aggregated measures and those measures would be repeated for each matching child row. | do NOT join to sibling aggregate views (e.g., monthly_sales_agg_by_product) on day without aligning grain (month vs day) — mismatched temporal grain will produce silently wrong rollups unless you aggregate or truncate to matching grain first. | If you need to combine this view with web_devices_totals (a normalized totals view) ensure the join keys include both day and channel (and letter if applicable) or aggregate the other side to day×letter×channel to avoid duplication or loss.
params.comparison: use web_demographics (base wide table) instead when you need the original wide columns or additional demographic columns that were not preserved here — web_demographics contains the source columns in wide form. | use web_devices_totals when you need device-level normalized totals (if that sibling contains device breakdowns not present here) — web_devices_totals may have different normalization and additional device keys. | use web_page_visit_counts or ticker_daily when you need different aggregated metrics or different grains (these siblings are aggregate views but over different measures/keys). For example, use ticker_daily for pure per-day time series of ticker metrics rather than per-channel/sex breakdowns. | do not substitute this view for orders_with_lines or purchases_enriched: those siblings are enriched/joined transactional views with different grains and identifiers (row-level or line-level), whereas this view represents pre-aggregated demographics metrics and lacks identifiers necessary for transactional joins.

views.description: Unpivots denormalized web_demographics into one row per day + gender + channel with cnt and qty measures. Useful to filter by gender or channel without parsing column names and to aggregate across channels/genders. | Use for: Aggregate demographics by gender or channel over time.; Join to channels_dim or gender_dim (channel_shortcut to channels_dim.shortcut) after mapping.

views.name: latest_purchase_per_product
views.body_sql:
SELECT id AS id,
       purchased AS purchased,
       brewery_id AS brewery_id,
       product_id AS product_id,
       qty AS qty,
       cost AS cost,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased DESC, id DESC) AS purchase_rank
FROM purchases

params.description: Returns the most recent purchase rows per product with a descending rank (1 = latest) computed over purchases.
params.when_to_use: Find the latest (or top-N) purchases for each product by purchase timestamp and id | Filter to purchase_rank = 1 to get a single latest purchase row per product | Enrich product-level datasets with the most recent purchase attributes (qty, cost, brewery_id) without aggregating across time
params.when_not_to_use: Joining this view to detail-level tables that are one-to-many on product (e.g., orders_with_lines) expecting sums — doing so can duplicate rows and inflate measures because this view remains at purchase-row grain (id). | Using this view to compute product lifetime aggregates (total qty sold, total revenue) — it only exposes individual purchase rows and a rank, not aggregates across purchases. | Assuming purchase_rank provides cohort membership across arbitrary windows — the rank is computed over all purchases in the purchases table (partition by product_id) and is not time-windowed, so cohorting by period requires re-computation or pre-filtering.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier of the purchase row; derives from purchases.id | purchased: purchase timestamp/datetime when the purchase occurred; derives from purchases.purchased | brewery_id: identifier of the brewery associated with that purchase row; derives from purchases.brewery_id | product_id: identifier of the product purchased; derives from purchases.product_id | qty: quantity purchased in that purchase row; derives from purchases.qty | cost: cost (monetary) for that purchase row; derives from purchases.cost | purchase_rank: RANK() of this purchase within its product partition ordered by purchased DESC, id DESC; 1 indicates the latest purchase for that product
params.grounded_columns: purchases.id | purchases.purchased | purchases.brewery_id | purchases.product_id | purchases.qty | purchases.cost
params.metric: purchase_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY purchases.product_id ORDER BY purchases.purchased DESC, purchases.id DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to products_dim on product_id (this view has at most one row per purchase id and product_id is the partition key for rank). Joining to products_dim (one row per product_id) is safe because products_dim is one-to-one on product_id and will not duplicate this view's rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to purchases_enriched on id (one-to-one join on purchase id) — safe because purchases_enriched should be at purchase-row grain and will not multiply rows if it is truly one-to-one. | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables keyed by product_id (for example orders_with_lines, inventory_by_location_product, monthly_sales_agg_by_product when those views are aggregated at a lower grain than a single row per product) without re-aggregating or deduplicating first, because those joins will multiply purchase rows and can cause over-counting of qty or cost. | do NOT join to raw purchase-level tables again (e.g., purchases) on product_id expecting to preserve uniqueness — joining to purchases on product_id would create a cartesian-like multiplication between this view's purchase rows and all purchases for that product, leading to inflated measures. If you need aggregated product-level metrics after joining to other purchase rows, aggregate (SUM/AVG) at the appropriate grain before joining.
params.comparison: use products_dim instead when you need canonical product attributes (name, category) because products_dim is a product-level dimension rather than purchase events. | use monthly_sales_agg_by_product instead when you need time-bucketed aggregated metrics (total qty or revenue per product per month) because that view provides pre-aggregated totals rather than per-purchase rows. | use purchases_enriched when you need purchase rows augmented with joined attributes (customer, location, derived flags) since purchases_enriched is likely a purchase-grain join and may already include additional contextual columns — latest_purchase_per_product only adds a rank and keeps raw purchase columns. | use inventory_by_location_product when you need on-hand inventory state by location and product — inventory is a different operational grain and should not be mixed with purchase event rows without clear re-aggregation or reconciliation.

views.description: Latest purchase event per product using purchased timestamp ordering. Exposes a rank so downstream queries can select latest (rank = 1). One row per purchase event with purchase_rank within product. | Use for: Find the most recent purchase for each product.; Compute supplier lead-times by comparing latest purchase to demand.
